stories.headline: Anthropic Launches 9 Creative Connectors Integrating Claude With Blender, Adobe, Autodesk, and More

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released nine MCP-based connectors partnering with Blender, Adobe, Autodesk Fusion, Ableton, Splice, Affinity by Canva, SketchUp, and Resolume (Arena and Wire).
The Adobe for creativity connector gives Claude access to 50+ tools across Creative Cloud apps including Photoshop, Premiere, Express, Illustrator, Firefly, and Lightroom.
The Autodesk Fusion connector lets designers and engineers create and modify 3D models through natural-language conversations with Claude.
The Blender connector provides a natural-language interface to Blender's Python API, and Anthropic joined the Blender Development Fund as a patron.
All connectors are built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), making them vendor-maintained and accessible to other large language models beyond Claude.

stories.headline: AWS Launches Amazon Quick Desktop App, a Proactive AI Assistant That Learns From Your Work

key_facts.fact: Amazon Quick is a desktop AI assistant that connects to local files, calendar, email, and apps like Google Workspace, Zoom, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and Slack.
Quick builds a personal knowledge graph from each user's interactions, becoming more personalized and proactive over time.
New integrations include Google Workspace, Zoom, Airtable, Dropbox, and Microsoft Teams, with free and Plus pricing plans requiring no AWS account.
Quick can proactively surface information — reminding users of unanswered emails, outstanding Salesforce deals, or documents requiring attention.
Announced at the 'What's Next with AWS' event, which also revealed OpenAI models GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 coming to Amazon Bedrock in limited preview.

stories.headline: China Suspends New Autonomous Driving Licenses After 100+ Baidu Robotaxis Stalled in Wuhan

key_facts.fact: China suspended issuing new licenses for autonomous vehicles after more than 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis suddenly stalled on Wuhan streets on March 31, stranding passengers and disrupting traffic
The suspension prevents self-driving companies from adding new robotaxis to their fleets, starting new test projects, or expanding into additional cities
Three agencies including China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology convened a meeting earlier in April with officials from cities that have robotaxi or autonomous-driving pilots
Baidu's Wuhan robotaxi operations have been suspended while local authorities investigate the incident; it is unclear how long the broader license suspension will last
Baidu Hong Kong shares fell about 4%, Pony.ai dropped 7%, and WeRide declined 3% on the news
Rival Pony.ai said its services in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen are operating normally; WeRide confirmed its services remain normal across 1,000+ square km

organizations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

stories.headline: Cognizant Acquires Data Center Infra Firm Astreya for ~$600M to Bolster AI Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Cognizant agreed to acquire Astreya, an AI-first IT managed services provider specializing in data center and AI infrastructure, for approximately $600 million

Founded in 2001, Astreya manages data center infrastructure, AI lab environments, and enterprise networks for six of the seven 'Magnificent Seven' hyperscalers, operating across 35+ countries with 2,200+ employees
The deal is Cognizant's fourth major acquisition in 18 months, following 3Cloud (Microsoft Azure, January 2026) and Belcan (digital engineering, 2024, ~$1.3B)
Astreya's proprietary AI OpsHub platform includes modules for readiness assessment, signal intelligence, analytics, and agentic automation
The deal is expected to close in Q2 2026 pending regulatory approvals; Cognizant, valued at $26 billion, has lost more than a third of its market value this year

stories.headline: 50+ Countries Open First Conference on Transitioning Away From Fossil Fuels in Colombia

key_facts.fact: More than 50 countries gathered in Santa Marta, Colombia for the First Conference on Transitioning away from Fossil Fuels, the political centerpiece of the event running April 28-29.
Colombian President Gustavo Petro warned the Amazon rainforest 'is burning' and the world could 'reach a point of no return,' questioning whether capitalism can adapt beyond fossil fuels.
Netherlands co-hosted the conference; Minister van Veldhoven said the transition 'strengthens our energy independence and security,' with Petro linking current conflicts to fossil fuel dependence.
Colombia's Environment Minister said the Middle East conflict revealed that 'we are not only dealing with a climate and environmental crisis, but also an economic and national security crisis.'

The conference will not produce binding agreements but aims to build political momentum outside the formal UN climate negotiation process; central challenge is funding the transition for developing countries.

stories.headline: EU Finds Meta in DSA Breach for Allowing Under-13 Users on Instagram and Facebook

key_facts.fact: The European Commission issued a preliminary finding that Meta's Instagram and Facebook are in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) for failing to prevent children under 13 from accessing the services.
Roughly 10-12% of children under 13 in the EU are using Instagram or Facebook, according to Commission findings, contradicting Meta's own internal assessments.
Children can enter a false date of birth when signing up with no mechanism to verify accuracy; Meta's reporting tool for under-13 users requires up to 7 clicks to access and is not pre-filled.
If confirmed, a non-compliance decision could trigger a fine of up to 6% of Meta's total worldwide annual turnover, potentially running into billions of euros.
Meta disagreed with the findings, saying age verification is an 'industry-wide challenge, which requires an industry-wide solution' and that it has measures to detect and remove underage accounts.

stories.headline: FIDO Alliance Forms AI Agent Working Groups; Google Donates Agent Payments Protocol to 60 Partners

key_facts.fact: The FIDO Alliance formed an Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group and a Payments Technical Working Group to develop standards for AI agent transactions.
Google donated the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) to FIDO and released AP2 v0.2 on GitHub, introducing 'Human Not Present' payments for autonomous agent transactions.
Mastercard co-developed Verifiable Intent, a tamper-proof log of user-authorized agent actions, also donated to FIDO alongside AP2.
60 organizations joined the initiative including Adyen, American Express, Ant International, Coinbase, Etsy, PayPal, Revolut, Salesforce, Visa, and Worldpay.
The Agentic Authentication Working Group is chaired by CVS Health, Google, and OpenAI, and vice-chaired by Amazon, Google, and Okta.
Some analysts estimate agentic commerce could reach $5 trillion globally by 2030, underscoring the urgency for payment and authentication standards.

stories.headline: Mayo Clinic AI System Detects Pancreatic Cancer on CT Scans 475 Days Before Diagnosis

key_facts.fact: Mayo Clinic researchers developed REDMOD (Radiomics-based Early Detection MODel), an AI system that identified pre-clinical pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma an average of 475 days (~15 months) before clinical diagnosis.
REDMOD achieved 73% sensitivity in detecting early-stage pancreatic cancer changes, nearly double the 39% sensitivity of experienced radiologists reviewing the same scans.
For cases detected more than 2 years before clinical diagnosis, REDMOD maintained 68% accuracy while radiologist detection fell to just 23%.
The study evaluated 219 routine CT scans from patients initially deemed cancer-free who later developed PDAC, plus 1,243 matched controls who remained cancer-free for 3+ years.
REDMOD correctly identified 88% of people who did not have pancreatic cancer and showed 90-92% consistency on repeat scans, demonstrating longitudinal reliability.

The research was published in the journal Gut and led by Ajit Harishkumar Goenka, MD, a researcher and clinician at Mayo Clinic. Pancreatic cancer has only about 13% five-year survival, largely due to late detection.

stories.headline: Nvidia Launches Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, Open Multimodal Model Unifying Vision, Audio, and Text

key_facts.fact: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni uses a 30B-A3B hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture with a 256K context length, combining vision and audio encoders into a single model.
The model tops six leaderboards for complex document intelligence and video/audio understanding, including MMlongbench-Doc, OCRBenchV2, WorldSense, DailyOmni, and VoiceBench.
The model delivers up to 9x higher throughput than other open omni models with the same interactivity, enabling lower-cost multimodal agent deployments.
Companies already adopting or evaluating the model include Foxconn, H Company, Palantir, Dell Technologies, Docusign, Infosys, and Oracle.
The Nemotron model family has seen over 50 million downloads in the past year.
On the OSWorld computer-use benchmark, Nemotron 3 Nano Omni scores 47.4 vs. 29.0 for Qwen3-Omni 30B-A3B, and on ScreenSpot-Pro GUI benchmark scores 57.8 vs. 59.7.

stories.headline: NXP Q1 Revenue Rises 12% to $3.18B, Beats Estimates as Auto and Industrial AI Demand Accelerates

key_facts.fact: NXP reported Q1 2026 revenue of $3.18 billion, up 12% year-over-year, beating the $3.15 billion consensus estimate by $31 million
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.05, exceeding guidance midpoint by $0.08; non-GAAP operating margin was 33.1%, up 120 basis points year-over-year
Automotive segment revenue was $1.78 billion (up 6% YoY, or 10% adjusted for the MEMS sensor business sale); Industrial & IoT surged 24% YoY to $628 million
Data center revenue exposure expected to surpass $500 million in 2026, up from $200 million in 2025
Company-specific growth drivers grew 18% year-over-year, comprising about one-third of total revenue, led by software-defined vehicles and physical AI
New industrial processing products (i.MX, RP, MCX) grew 75% year-over-year and represented almost half of the Industrial & IoT segment growth

stories.headline: Pentagon Signs Google Gemini Deal for Classified Work, Expanding AI Vendor Base

key_facts.fact: Pentagon AI chief Cameron Stanley confirmed the DoD is expanding its use of Google's Gemini AI model, including for classified projects, about two months after blacklisting Anthropic as a supply chain risk.

Google signed the classified-work deal with the DoD on Monday, April 28. The agreement allows essentially all lawful uses, making Google the third AI firm (after OpenAI and xAI) to fill the Anthropic void.
'Overreliance on one vendor is never a good thing,' Stanley said, adding that Gemini is 'saving thousands of man hours, literally thousands of man hours on a weekly basis.'

Anthropic is excluded from DoD contracts after a D.C. appeals court denied its request to block the blacklisting, but a San Francisco judge granted a separate injunction allowing it to work with other agencies.

Over 700 Google employees signed a letter to CEO Sundar Pichai calling for the company to reject classified workloads, saying they don't want the technology 'used in inhumane or extremely harmful ways.'
Stanley said Anthropic's Mythos rollout was a 'wakeup call' and the DoD is 'taking this very seriously' to be 'prepared for what comes next, which is a whole raft of AI-enabled capabilities.'

stories.headline: Poolside Launches Laguna XS.2 Open-Weight and M.1 Proprietary Models for Agentic Coding

key_facts.fact: Laguna XS.2 is a 33B-parameter MoE model with 3B active parameters, released under Apache 2.0 license, designed for local agentic coding.
Laguna M.1 is a proprietary 225B-parameter MoE model with 23B active parameters, optimized for complex, long-horizon software engineering problems.
Both models were trained from scratch in-house using Poolside's Muon optimizer, not fine-tuned from existing open-source models like Qwen.
Poolside also launched 'pool', a coding agent harness, and 'shimmer', a web-based interactive preview environment for agentic coding on the go.
The Laguna architecture features per-layer head counts and a sigmoid MoE router with auxiliary-loss-free load balancing.
M.1 is being offered free temporarily through Poolside's API and distribution partners OpenRouter, Ollama, and Baseten.

stories.headline: Seagate Q3 Revenue Surges 44% to $3.11B on AI Storage Demand, Guides Q4 Far Above Estimates

key_facts.fact: Seagate reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $3.11 billion, up 44% year-over-year and 10% sequentially, beating the $2.96 billion estimate
Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.10, up 115% year-over-year from $1.90; GAAP diluted EPS was $3.27 versus $1.57 a year earlier
Data center revenue reached $2.5 billion, up 55% year-over-year, with data center exabyte shipments at 175 EB, up 47% YoY
Free cash flow reached $953 million, up 57% quarter-over-quarter, the highest level in over a decade; free cash flow margin reached 31%
Seagate guided Q4 revenue of $3.45 billion ± $100M versus $3.16B estimate, and adjusted EPS of $5.00 ± $0.20 versus $3.97 estimate
Shares surged around 16% in after-hours trading, also lifting Western Digital (+11%) and SanDisk (+4%); Fitch upgraded Seagate's credit rating to investment grade
Nearline capacity is almost fully allocated through calendar 2027, with build-to-order contracts finalized through fiscal 2027

stories.headline: TSMC Fully Exits Arm Holdings With $231M Share Sale, Doubling Its Original Investment

key_facts.fact: TSMC's subsidiary sold its remaining 1.11 million Arm shares at $207.65 each from April 28-29, totaling approximately $231 million
TSMC no longer holds any Arm shares after the transaction, completing a full exit from the position
TSMC originally invested about $100 million in Arm at $51 per share during Arm's 2023 IPO, making the exit at ~$208 roughly a quadrupling of the IPO price
The disposal resulted in a $174 million impact on retained earnings
TSMC had been gradually reducing its stake, having previously sold 850,000 shares in 2024 at $119.47 each for about $102 million
Arm shares fell 7.98% on Tuesday as TSMC completed the sale

stories.headline: UAE Exits OPEC and OPEC+ After Nearly 60 Years, Stripping Cartel of Third-Largest Producer

key_facts.fact: The UAE announced on April 28 it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, after nearly 60 years of membership through Abu Dhabi (joined 1967).
The UAE was producing around 3.4 million barrels per day before the Iran war, but has capacity to produce roughly 5 million bpd. OPEC quotas limited it to 3.2 million bpd.
Energy Minister Suhail Al Mazrouei said the exit was timed to minimize disruption, as the Strait of Hormuz closure limits exports. UAE aims for 5 million bpd capacity by 2027.
The UAE's departure reduces OPEC's control of global supply from about 30% to 26%, and removes one of its few members with meaningful spare production capacity.
Oil markets barely reacted: Brent crude traded above $111 a barrel (50%+ above prewar price), driven by the Strait of Hormuz closure rather than the OPEC announcement.
The exit caps years of tension with Saudi Arabia over oil quotas and regional political influence, including a rift over Yemen security policy in December 2025.
The UAE's withdrawal affects roughly 12% of OPEC's total oil output, far more significant than Qatar (2019) or Angola (2024) departures.

stories.headline: US Orders Chip Equipment Companies to Halt Shipments to China's No. 2 Chipmaker Hua Hong

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department last week sent letters to multiple chip equipment companies ordering them to halt certain tool shipments to Hua Hong, China's second-largest contract chipmaker
Lam Research, Applied Materials, and KLA — top US chip equipment companies with significant China business — were among those believed to have received the restriction letters

The restrictions target Hua Hong facilities that US officials believe may produce China's most advanced chips, including Huali Microelectronics which was preparing a 7-nanometer chipmaking process at its Shanghai plant
Shares of KLA fell 4.7%, Applied Materials dropped 5.8%, and Lam Research closed down 3.1% on April 28; Hua Hong shares lost 3.5%
The move could increase US-China tension ahead of President Trump's scheduled meeting with President Xi Jinping in Beijing in May
SMIC is currently the only Chinese company that can make chips with 7nm technologies; Hua Hong's Huali was developing comparable capability
